facts.fact: The South African Reserve Bank directive says low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area (Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa) are currently executed through SADC-RTGS.

The South African Reserve Bank directive says Common Monetary Area low-value transfers, including this country's, run through the SADC-RTGS regional system and must move to the TCIB scheme by April 2027.
The directive says low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area are currently executed through SADC-RTGS.
Eswatini payment service providers route low-value CMA cross-border transfers through the SADC-RTGS system and must move them to the TCIB scheme by 31 March 2027.
Independent News reports that MTN Eswatini launched its MoMo Cross-Border Service on 2 December 2024, letting MTN customers in South Africa send money directly to MoMo wallets in Eswatini.

facts.fact: The CMA Cross-border Payments Oversight Committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says rand cross-border low-value EFTs within the Common Monetary Area, including Eswatini, run through an interim supplementary-file solution in place since 1 October 2019 and still in use.

The CMA committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says banks route low-value cross-border EFTs within the CMA, Eswatini among its four members, through the SADC real-time gross settlement system under the interim arrangement, to move to a designated retail system such as TCIB from 1 April 2027.

The South African Reserve Bank said that from 30 September 2024 low-value electronic funds transfers, debit and credit payments among Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa are treated as cross-border transactions with greater due diligence.
